name: Redis
description: Protects against destructive Redis operations like FLUSHALL, \ FLUSHDB, and mass key deletion

destructive_patterns.name: stdin-unverified
destructive_patterns.description: redis-cli receives indirect input that the engine cannot statically verify.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Materialize and review the exact Redis commands before piping or redirecting them into the client.

destructive_patterns.name: flushall
destructive_patterns.description: FLUSHALL permanently deletes ALL keys in ALL databases.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
FLUSHALL removes every key from every database (0-15 by default):

\ - All cached data is lost \ - All session data is gone \ - All queues are emptied \ - Affects ALL databases, not just current

\ This is instant and cannot be undone. RDB/AOF backups are not affected \ until the next save.

\ Check database sizes first: \ INFO keyspace \ DBSIZE

\ Consider: \ FLUSHDB # Only current database \ DEL key1 key2 # Specific keys

destructive_patterns.name: flushdb
destructive_patterns.description: FLUSHDB permanently deletes ALL keys in the current database.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
FLUSHDB removes all keys from the currently selected database:

\ - All keys in this database are deleted \ - Other databases (0-15) are unaffected \ - Instant execution, no confirmation \ - Cannot be undone

\ Check current database and key count: \ CLIENT INFO # Shows current DB \ DBSIZE # Keys in current DB \ KEYS '*' | head -20 # Sample keys (slow on large DBs)

\ Prefer audited per-key cleanup with a dry run and backup.

destructive_patterns.name: config-resetstat
destructive_patterns.description: CONFIG RESETSTAT clears Redis runtime counters and can hide recent incidents.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
CONFIG RESETSTAT resets Redis statistics reported by INFO:

\ - Command counters and error counters are cleared \ - Recent operational evidence can be lost \ - Capacity and incident analysis becomes harder

\ Capture INFO and monitoring data first, then run this manually only when \ resetting observability counters is intentional.

destructive_patterns.name: mass-delete-pipeline
destructive_patterns.description: Redis KEYS/SCAN piped to DEL/UNLINK can delete many keys at once.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Piping Redis key enumeration into DEL or UNLINK can delete every matching key:

\ - redis-cli KEYS '*' | xargs redis-cli DEL removes all returned keys \ - redis-cli --scan --pattern 'prefix:*' | xargs redis-cli UNLINK removes a whole key namespace \ - This bypasses Redis's lack of wildcard DEL by expanding keys client-side

\ Safer alternatives: \ redis-cli --scan --pattern 'prefix:*' | head -50 # inspect first \ Count and back up affected keys before selective deletion \ Prefer application-owned cleanup tooling with dry-run support

destructive_patterns.name: debug-crash
destructive_patterns.description: DEBUG SEGFAULT/CRASH will crash the Redis server.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
DEBUG SEGFAULT/CRASH intentionally crashes the Redis server:

\ - Server process terminates immediately \ - All connections are dropped \ - Unsaved data may be lost \ - Services depending on Redis fail

\ This is meant for testing crash recovery, not production use.

\ These commands should be disabled in production: \ CONFIG SET debug-command no \ rename-command DEBUG "" # In redis.conf

destructive_patterns.name: debug-sleep
destructive_patterns.description: DEBUG SLEEP blocks the Redis server and can cause availability issues.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
DEBUG SLEEP blocks the Redis server for the specified duration:

\ - All client connections freeze \ - No commands are processed \ - Cluster may mark node as failed \ - Can trigger failover in Sentinel setups

\ This is meant for testing timeouts, not production use.

\ Disable in production: \ CONFIG SET debug-command no

destructive_patterns.name: shutdown
destructive_patterns.description: SHUTDOWN stops the Redis server. SHUTDOWN NOSAVE risks data loss.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
SHUTDOWN stops the Redis server:

\ - SHUTDOWN SAVE: Saves RDB before exit (default) \ - SHUTDOWN NOSAVE: Exits immediately, no save \ - All client connections are closed \ - Services depending on Redis fail

\ Check for unsaved changes: \ INFO persistence # Look at rdb_changes_since_last_save

\ Ensure proper restart mechanism exists (systemd, Docker, etc.).

destructive_patterns.name: config-dangerous
destructive_patterns.description: CONFIG SET for dir/dbfilename/slaveof can be used for security attacks.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
These CONFIG SET options are commonly exploited in Redis attacks:

\ - dir + dbfilename: Can write arbitrary files (RCE vector) \ - slaveof/replicaof: Can exfiltrate data to attacker's server

\ Attack example: \ 1. CONFIG SET dir /var/spool/cron \ 2. CONFIG SET dbfilename root \ 3. SET payload '* * * * * malicious-command' \ 4. BGSAVE

\ Disable in production: \ rename-command CONFIG "" # In redis.conf

\ Use ACLs to restrict these commands.

destructive_patterns.name: config-set-maxmemory
destructive_patterns.description: CONFIG SET maxmemory can trigger immediate mass key eviction if new limit is below current usage.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Lowering maxmemory below current usage causes Redis to evict keys immediately \ according to the active eviction policy:

\ - volatile-lru/allkeys-lru: Silently deletes keys to fit budget \ - noeviction: Returns OOM errors on writes

\ Check current usage first: \ INFO memory # Look at used_memory vs maxmemory

\ Prefer gradual reduction or off-peak changes.

destructive_patterns.name: config-set-maxmemory-policy
destructive_patterns.description: CONFIG SET maxmemory-policy changes how Redis evicts keys, risking silent data loss.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Switching eviction policy can silently delete keys:

\ - noeviction -> allkeys-lru: Enables silent key deletion \ - volatile-* -> allkeys-*: Extends eviction to non-expiring keys

\ Check current policy: \ CONFIG GET maxmemory-policy

\ Ensure application logic handles the new eviction behavior.

destructive_patterns.name: config-set-save
destructive_patterns.description: CONFIG SET save can disable RDB persistence entirely, risking data loss on restart.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
CONFIG SET save "" disables all RDB snapshots:

\ - No automatic persistence to disk \ - All data lost on restart unless AOF is enabled \ - Existing RDB file may become stale

\ Check current persistence: \ CONFIG GET save \ CONFIG GET appendonly

\ Ensure at least one persistence mechanism remains active.

destructive_patterns.name: config-set-appendonly
destructive_patterns.description: CONFIG SET appendonly can disable AOF persistence, risking data loss on restart.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Disabling AOF without RDB means zero persistence:

\ - CONFIG SET appendonly no: Stops AOF logging \ - Combined with disabled RDB: complete data loss on crash/restart

\ Check other persistence mechanisms: \ CONFIG GET save \ CONFIG GET appendonly

\ Ensure at least one persistence mechanism remains active.

destructive_patterns.name: config-rewrite
destructive_patterns.description: CONFIG REWRITE persists all runtime CONFIG SET changes to redis.conf permanently.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
CONFIG REWRITE writes current runtime config back to redis.conf:

\ - Makes all CONFIG SET changes survive restarts \ - Can persist dangerous temporary changes permanently \ - No undo: must manually edit redis.conf to revert

\ Review current runtime changes first: \ CONFIG GET * # Compare with original redis.conf

\ Ensure no dangerous CONFIG SET changes are pending before rewriting.
